qs.q: A 52-year-old man presents with black, tarry stools of three days' duration. Hemodynamic vitals are stable and digital rectal examination confirms dark guaiac-positive stool. The passage of melena in this patient most reliably points to which source?
qs.e: Melena requires degradation of hemoglobin by intestinal bacteria, typically indicating a source proximal to the ligament of Treitz. A lower GI source or rapid transit usually results in hematochezia rather than dark tarry stools.

qs.q: A 50-year-old man presents with fever, chills, dysuria, and a tender, boggy prostate on digital rectal exam. Urine cultures grow common uropathogens. What is the most fitting classification and management approach for this patient?
qs.e: Acute bacterial prostatitis presents with systemic symptoms, dysuria, and a tender boggy prostate, and is managed with antibiotics. Chronic nonbacterial prostatitis lacks proven therapy and represents the majority of chronic pelvic pain syndrome cases.
qs.s: Quick Guide: Male Reproductive System Pathology, Testis, Penis: MCQs

qs.q: A 70-year-old man is evaluated for metastatic bone pain and a hard, nodular prostate gland on digital rectal examination. Elevation of which serum enzyme historically marked this suspected malignancy?
qs.e: Serum acid phosphatase was historically used as a classic diagnostic marker for prostatic carcinoma. Alkaline phosphatase is predominantly elevated in bone and liver disorders.
qs.s: Specific Proteins in Clinical Diagnosis: MCQs

qs.q: A 68-year-old man presents with urinary hesitancy, nocturia, and a uniformly enlarged, firm prostate on digital rectal examination. Which active androgen metabolite is primarily responsible for mediating the proliferation of glandular and stromal tissue in this condition?
qs.e: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is driven primarily by dihydrotestosterone, which binds nuclear receptors with higher affinity than testosterone. Testosterone serves as the precursor but undergoes local conversion via 5-alpha-reductase within the prostate stroma.
qs.s: Female & Male Genital Pathology: Ulcers, HPV, Endometriosis,: MCQs

qs.q: An elderly patient is diagnosed with prostate carcinoma. Where within the prostate gland does prostate carcinoma most commonly arise, allowing it to be palpable on a digital rectal examination?
qs.e: Prostate carcinoma typically arises in the peripheral zone (posterior lobe) of the prostate, making it accessible to palpation during a digital rectal exam. This differs from BPH, which arises in the transition zone.
qs.s: Female & Male Genital Pathology: Ulcers, HPV, Endometriosis,: MCQs

qs.q: A 45-year-old man presents with fever, chills, dysuria, and a tender, boggy prostate on digital rectal examination. Laboratory workup confirms acute bacterial prostatitis. What is the approximate frequency of this specific category among all diagnosed cases of prostatitis?
o: Accounting for 2 to 5 percent of cases
Accounting for 10 to 15 percent of cases
Accounting for 90 to 95 percent of cases
Accounting for 50 to 60 percent of cases
qs.e: Acute bacterial prostatitis and chronic bacterial prostatitis each account for about 2 to 5 percent of prostatitis cases. Chronic nonbacterial prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome is by far the most frequent, making up 90 to 95 percent of cases.
qs.s: Penile & Testicular Pathologies: Hypospadias, Tumors, Torsion – Male: MCQs

qs.q: A 52-year-old male presents with fever, chills, dysuria, and a tender, boggy prostate upon digital rectal examination. Urine cultures confirm acute bacterial prostatitis. What is the approximate frequency of this specific category among all prostatitis cases?
qs.e: Acute and chronic bacterial prostatitis each account for only 2 to 5 percent of all prostatitis cases. The vast majority of cases belong to chronic nonbacterial prostatitis or chronic pelvic pain syndrome.
qs.s: Male Reproductive Pathology: Comprehensive Review: MCQs

qs.q: A 38-year-old man presents with perineal pain, pain on ejaculation, and tenderness upon digital rectal examination of the prostate. What is the most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Prostatitis is suggested by perineal or suprapubic pain, pain on ejaculation, and prostatic tenderness on rectal examination. These specific local symptoms distinguish it from generalized cystitis or urethritis.
